headline: Over 400 American AI Data Centers Use As Much Electricity As Wisconsin, Michigan, or Indiana
claim: The largest U.S. data centers emit as much carbon as Denmark.
notes: published 2026-11-16; Nature Sustainability study by Harvard researchers (403 US hyperscale data centers, May 2024 to April 2025); reports about 25.7 million metric tons CO2 and states that emissions are estimated from regional grid mix; estimate, not a company's own numbers; the article's headline is about electricity use

headline: Harvard study: Largest U.S. data centers emit more carbon than all of Denmark
claim: The largest U.S. data centers emit as much carbon as Denmark.
notes: published 2026-11-16; coverage of the Harvard-led Nature Sustainability study; estimate, not a measurement of each facility; the study window ends April 2025

headline: ‘AI rebounding’: Nearly 20% of U.S. workers replaced by AI are being asked back—now they’re demanding higher pay, job security and AI transparency
claim: Workers replaced by AI are being asked back to their jobs.
notes: published 2026-11-09; Fortune story republished on Yahoo Finance; survey commissioned by SHL, a talent-assessment firm (interested party), fieldwork June to July 2026; 19.1% of US respondents said they were replaced by AI and later asked to return; survey measures self-report, not company records
